extracted.intended_audience: general readers and researchers interested in technology media companies, journalists, and media analysts
extracted.subtask_description: Identify and assess criteria used to judge the trustworthiness, editorial practices, and product safety of a technology news website (example: CNET). Focuses on editorial integrity, AI use, advertiser influence, content retention, and download safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial content quality and factual reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: CNET 'faced criticism for what was described as a decline in quality of its editorial content and factual reliability due to the use of generative AI in the creation of its articles.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure whether articles are factually accurate, free of serious errors, and uphold traditional journalistic standards. Anti-patterns: publishing content that contains 'serious errors' or inaccurate information (noted in reviews of CNET's AI-era articles). Scoring notes: downgraded reliability when multiple errors are found or when independent reviewers flag widespread issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and disclosure of AI-generated content
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism that CNET 'failed to disclose that it was using a machine to write articles' and that some AI-generated content was published without clear disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the publisher clearly states when content is generated or substantially produced by AI, and whether policies on AI use are public and followed. Examples/anti-patterns: using human bylines on AI-written pieces until detected; claiming 'not actively using AI' while evidence shows AI publication. Good practice: public AI policy and upfront disclosure on affected articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism avoidance, editorial review, and correction processes
rubrics_metrics.description: CNET 'reviewed those articles... after many were found to contain serious errors and plagiarized material.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the outlet has processes to detect plagiarism, review flagged content, correct mistakes, and retract or amend problematic pieces. Anti-patterns: publishing plagiarized material, delayed or absent corrections. Guidance: timely review of flagged AI-written work and transparent correction notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalistic independence from advertisers and sponsored content influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerns over 'journalistic integrity regarding increased publication of slanted reviews and sponsored content to benefit its advertising partners' and staff statements that management 'pushed them to give more favourable coverage to advertisers.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the separation between editorial and commercial/sponsored content, disclosure of sponsorships, and evidence of editorial direction favoring advertisers. Anti-patterns: slanted reviews, undisclosed sponsored content, editorial pressure to favor advertisers. Scoring notes: documented staff complaints or patterns of favorable coverage lower the independence score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest management in reviews and awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: the 'Hopper controversy' where CBS disqualified Dish Network's Hopper from CNET's CES 'Best in Show' because CBS was in litigation with Dish, prompting criticism and changes to award governance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the organization identifies, discloses, and manages conflicts of interest (especially for awards, reviews, and editorial decisions). Anti-patterns: allowing corporate legal/financial relationships to override staff votes or editorial judgment; withholding disclosure of conflicts. Good practice: recusal, transparent procedures, and transferring award decision authority when conflicts exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Byline integrity and author attribution (including consent when AI edits articles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances where employees demanded removal of their bylines 'to protect her reputation if her articles were revised by AI' and use of human bylines on AI-generated content until caught.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess policies around who receives bylines, whether authors can opt out if content is AI-altered, and whether bylines truthfully reflect authorship. Anti-patterns: attributing AI-written work to staff without consent; failing to correct bylines when content origin changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content retention, archiving practices, and SEO ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: CNET 'deleted thousands of old articles... in an effort to raise the search engine optimization rankings on Google Search'; CNET creates an internal copy and Wayback Machine copy and alerts writers 10 days in advance, while Google said deleting articles to optimize rankings is not a good practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the outlet preserves historical content for accountability, documents deletions transparently, and avoids manipulative SEO practices. Good practices: internal archiving, public explanation for deletions, notifying affected authors. Anti-patterns: mass deletions primarily to manipulate search rankings without transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety and trustworthiness of downloadable content and platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Regarding Download.com: 'CNET claims that this software is free of spyware, but independent sources have confirmed that this is not the case... some downloads do contain malware.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the security screening processes for downloadable files, accuracy of safety claims, and transparency about risks. Anti-patterns: bundling bloatware/malware with installers, claiming absolute safety while independent analyses contradict that. Guidance: independent audits, clear user warnings, and rapid remediation when unsafe packages are discovered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment practices and newsroom treatment affecting credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Following the AI and editorial controversies, '10% of CNET staff were laid off' and 'employees unionized in response to the scandal and layoffs,' with staff arguing AI posed a danger to reputations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how layoffs, unionization, and staff treatment reflect on editorial stability and moral authority. While not a direct content-quality metric, poor labor practices and staff pushback can signal systemic editorial problems. Examples: staff resignations over editorial interference, calls to remove bylines to protect reputations.
